title: Full faithfulness and essential image of ordinary Dieudonné crystals
as_he_states: Problem1 asks full faithfulness on every characteristic-p base and whether its image is precisely the admissible FV-crystals; the proposed admissibility is existence of the canonical direct-summand Hodge filtration.
plausible_today: Retain the exact base and the precise extra structures: perfect-ring Dieudonné equivalence, excellent lci full faithfulness, or the quasi-syntomic prismatic equivalence are established formulations. Ordinary crystals on arbitrary bases cannot be assumed fully faithful.
state_of_art: As of2026-11-19: de Jong ICM1998 §2(x) explicitly records the Berthelot–Messing counterexample over Fp[x,y]/(x²,xy,y²). Lau6.4 settles perfect rings; de Jong–Messing1999 gives excellent-lci full faithfulness; Anschütz–Le Bras1.4.4 gives quasi-syntomic prismatic classification. Their structures/hypotheses differ.
why_open: The manuscript says the missing finite-flat theory would clarify the problem. The published counterexample explains failure of the unrestricted hope; no historical reason for abandonment beyond that is inferred.
worth: Worth a focused comparison of the handwritten admissibility condition with precise divided/prismatic data, because simply citing modern classification hides the lost hypotheses.

title: Finite flat and truncated Dieudonné theory
as_he_states: Develop a theory for arbitrary finite locally free p-groups, possibly using a filtration on a derived object; over perfect S, give the anti-equivalence for groups flat over Z/p^n and locally free Witt modules with usual FV conditions.
plausible_today: Over perfect rings use admissible torsion Dieudonné modules for all finite p-groups and level-n projective Dieudonné modules with the exact level-one kernel/image and projectivity conditions for truncated BT groups. Over broader bases extra divided/prismatic structure is essential.
state_of_art: Lau2013 Definition6.1, Theorem6.4 and Corollary6.5 give exact perfect-ring categories. Anschütz–Le Bras2023 §5.1 treats finite locally free p-primary groups in the quasi-syntomic setting.
why_open: The text expressly says the additional structures have not been isolated and speculates about a derived filtration. No identification with a modern construction is asserted without a comparison.
worth: Worth an expository reconstruction of the category distinction; a few hours can establish an exact dictionary, not a new arbitrary-base classification.

title: Deformation theory for finite flat p-groups
as_he_states: Find a variant of the BT deformation theorem for finite locally free p-groups; the margin says there is a candidate but supplies none.
plausible_today: Fix a finite flat/truncated-BT category and nilpotent PD thickening; formulate deformations with the extra structures required by a chosen established theory. The unwritten candidate cannot be recovered uniquely.
state_of_art: Illusie1985 reconstructs Grothendieck’s truncated-BT deformation theorem and discusses the proof route. Anschütz–Le Bras §5.1 provides a later finite-flat classification on quasi-syntomic bases, rather than a theorem on every base mentioned by the manuscript.
why_open: Illusie’s introduction explicitly explains how Raynaud’s local embedding result simplifies the route through BBM; the source itself says only that a candidate exists.
worth: Worth locating the candidate in adjacent seminar material before proposing any new theorem, because the present leaf does not determine its statement.

title: Nilpotent invariance up to isogeny and global bounds
as_he_states: Prove later that restriction across a nilpotent immersion induces equivalence on the globally localized BT categories; quasi-compactness is cancelled and the phrase power of J is doubtful.
plausible_today: Require a single p-power annihilating the ideal, as in the published theorem, or formulate a genuinely local quasi-isogeny category and prove its descent. Local denominators do not glue automatically in Hom⊗Q.
state_of_art: GrothICM1970 §5 p434 gives the bounded-p-ideal theorem. Katz1.1.3 proves uniform lifting of multiples. The disjoint-union example in proof_checks.md independently shows global Hom localization is not a stack.
why_open: The page itself flags the stack defect; no source explains why quasi-compactness was cancelled. The mathematical issue is a global denominator bound, not a visual decision about the cancellation.
worth: High value for the companion: fix the exact global category and inspect the p/J glyph before quoting the invariance theorem.

title: Essential image, valuative testing and Zariski openness
as_he_states: Characterize realizable filtered isocrystals over noetherian p-adically complete rings; ask for a valuative criterion and a Zariski-open Grassmannian locus of admissible two-step filtrations.
plausible_today: Over a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with perfect residue field, weak admissibility is the exact rational criterion; period-domain families require a specified analytic topology and a distinction between classical and general analytic points. A general Zariski-open locus is a different statement.
state_of_art: Colmez–Fontaine §4.1 Theorem4.3 proves weakly admissible equals admissible for filtered(phi,N)-modules over the stated valued fields. Hartl2008 Theorems1.2,3.3,3.5 and Example3.6 give analytic loci and their strict difference at nonclassical points with fixed residue field Fp-bar. These do not settle the exact universal Zariski/valuative wording.
why_open: The manuscript acknowledges that rank conditions are insufficient. The sources show why field-point criteria do not automatically identify the relative analytic space; no claim of worldwide openness is made for every reformulation.
worth: Worth isolating the smallest exact Zariski claim and an explicit isocrystal example before expanding the relative question.

title: The mysterious period functor and its inverse
as_he_states: Construct explicitly the natural Galois realization of a realizable filtered isocrystal and a quasi-inverse; the local cancellation on48 does not cancel the surviving later questions.
plausible_today: For K complete mixed-characteristic discretely valued with perfect residue field, use D_cris and V_cris on crystalline Qp representations and weakly admissible filtered isocrystals. A rational functor does not choose a Zp lattice.
state_of_art: Colmez–Fontaine Theorem4.3 and its corollary give the semistable equivalence; the N=0 subcategory is crystalline. The source’s two-step BT setting is a restricted weight range, not every filtered isocrystal.
why_open: The text calls the construction mysterious but gives no sociological reason for delay. Later period-ring methods give the precise algebraic answer.
worth: Worth a compact notation dictionary from the page to the period-ring functors, including covariance and twists.

title: Relative p-adic local systems from filtered crystals
as_he_states: For general noetherian p-adically complete A, map realizable filtered isocrystals to p-adic locally constant sheaves on Spec(A[1/p]), allowing unspecified additional conditions.
plausible_today: State the base and linear category precisely; for quasi-syntomic bases use prismatic Dieudonné crystals and their étale realization. Pointwise Galois representations alone do not provide transport/descent.
state_of_art: Anschütz–Le Bras §5.4 Proposition5.4.2 identifies the Frobenius-fixed prismatic realization with the dual finite-level generic-fibre local system of a BT group on the associated adic v-site. This is an exact modern relative construction but in a different specified formalism.
why_open: No historical reason is documented. The mathematical obstruction to an immediate fieldwise solution is compatibility over the base and the essential-image conditions.
worth: Worth comparing sites and covariance for one formally smooth affine base; a few hours can establish a reliable example rather than every noetherian-base theorem.

title: Which Galois lattices arise from BT groups?
as_he_states: Determine the essential image in Galois modules; Hodge–Tate conditions are recorded as necessary, followed by the filtered-crystal inverse question.
plausible_today: Separate integral Zp lattices, rational crystalline representations and Hodge–Tate representations. Hodge–Tate alone is insufficient; the precise integral BT criterion needs an integral crystalline theory and specified weights.
state_of_art: Tate1967 §4 Theorem3 establishes the Hodge–Tate decomposition for BT groups. Colmez–Fontaine gives rational crystalline admissibility. Anschütz–Le Bras gives the integral BT classification on quasi-syntomic bases and its generic-fibre comparison.
why_open: The source does not claim Hodge–Tate sufficiency; no explanation of abandonment is present.
worth: Worth an exact integral-versus-rational comparison with the source’s covariance convention; this prevents a false claim that rational periods recover a unique lattice.

title: Tate full faithfulness in equal characteristic
as_he_states: Remove the characteristic-zero function-field restriction in Tate’s generic-fibre full-faithfulness theorem on normal noetherian integral bases.
plausible_today: The same BT full-faithfulness conclusion holds with no characteristic restriction; normality and the noetherian condition remain.
state_of_art: de Jong1998 Corollary1.2 proves the DVR characteristic-p case; its introduction explains the reduction to this case. de Jong ICM1998 Theorem2 states the normal noetherian integral-base conclusion. The1999 erratum corrects an auxiliary lemma/definition and leaves these theorem statements unchanged.
why_open: The manuscript proposes a crystalline route conditionally. The1998 proof establishes the missing theorem; the erratum identifies an actual kernel issue rather than a failure of full faithfulness.
worth: Settled: worth documenting the exact1998 theorem and1999 correction, not recasting it as an open research direction.

title: Generic restriction for ordinary locally free crystals
as_he_states: Is generic restriction fully faithful for all locally free crystals over a normal noetherian integral characteristic-p base?
plausible_today: A theorem must specify the crystalline site, integrality/isogeny level and any convergence hypotheses. Do not infer it by forgetting the Frobenius condition in a theorem for F-crystals.
state_of_art: de Jong1998 Theorem1.1 concerns nondegenerate F-crystals over a characteristic-p DVR with a p-basis. Searches of Numdam, arXiv, zbMATH-indexed results and backward references did not identify an exact theorem or a complete counterexample for the broader ordinary-crystal wording.
why_open: The source immediately offers the weaker F-crystal question. That indicates awareness of a possible missing structure; no further reason is documented.
worth: Worth a precise local restatement and a low-rank extension/counterexample search, because the current broad question is not answered by the cited F-crystal theorem.

title: Generic restriction for F-crystals
as_he_states: At least establish the generic full-faithfulness statement for F-crystals.
plausible_today: For a DVR of characteristic p admitting a p-basis and nondegenerate Frobenius, generic restriction of F-crystals is fully faithful. A global extension beyond that setting needs its own reduction theorem.
state_of_art: de Jong1998 Theorem1.1 is the exact local theorem; de JongICM1998 §1 defines nondegenerate as kernel and cokernel killed by a p-power. The erratum does not modify Theorem1.1.
why_open: The page weakens the question but does not supply a proof; later crystalline analysis addresses the local case.
worth: Worth recording the p-basis and nondegeneracy qualifiers in the companion; broader research should start from the precise local/global gap.

title: Reduction to formal connections and the perfect closure
as_he_states: Reduce to a one-variable complete local ring over an algebraically closed field, express crystals as modules with formal connections, and descend from the perfection using a faithful Dieudonné theory.
plausible_today: Keep quasi-nilpotence, continuity, the crystalline lift and horizontal nondegenerate Frobenius; k[[t]] must be distinguished from k((t)). The group theorem’s reduction does not automatically establish all ordinary-crystal variants.
state_of_art: Berthelot–Messing1979 §1 Lemma1 describes the perfect-closure strategy and its field case; de Jong1998 introduction gives the precise Tate reduction and Theorem1.1 the F-crystal result. Lau6.4 supplies perfect-ring classification.
why_open: The source explicitly makes the route conditional on Problem1 and says it seems to imply the desired result. No completed reduction is printed there.
worth: Worth a dependency diagram with each category and local hypothesis; the first concrete task is to collate the Laurent/power-series glyph.

title: Exponential construction and crystalline universal extensions
as_he_states: Construct transitive canonical identifications between universal extensions of different lifts; explain the exponential lifting of vector subgroups, the abelian quotient and the comparison with the cohomological BT construction.
plausible_today: Use locally nilpotent divided powers for the deformation equivalence and the precise universal-extension/sheaf sites. The vector extension and its Lie crystal must remain distinct objects.
state_of_art: de Jong1995 introduction pp5–6 attributes the exponential construction to Messing and its comparison with degree-one abelian cohomology to Mazur–Messing. Illusie Pisa §5 describes the universal-extension mechanism and its historical letters. The exact R¹crys Gm notation requires site/convention collation. Exact own-published parallel now collated: GrothMontreal1974 V§4 pp116–118, including char0 unique marked smooth-group lifting of E(A); the full nil-thickening proof is carried from that published assertion, not independently reproduced here.
why_open: These pages explicitly defer the two constructions and mark the abelian-to-BT passage heuristic; the later sources document how they were developed.
worth: Worth a faithful comparison of the two constructions and the A/A-dual conventions, rather than claiming the short quotient paragraph is already a proof.

title: The deformation theorem and its nilpotence qualifications
as_he_states: Lift BT groups by lifting their Hodge direct summands; the inserted qualification allows nilpotent divided powers or a connected group/connected dual.
plausible_today: Retain one of those qualifications and marked deformation data; do not replace the categorical theorem by uniqueness of an unmarked lift.
state_of_art: GrothICM1970 §4 pp433–434 states the qualified theorem and Remark1 gives failure without the hypotheses even for an ordinary split height-two group. de Jong1995 Proposition3.2.1 invokes MessingV1.6 in the nilpotent-PD form; Katz1.2.1 supplies Serre–Tate.
why_open: The correction is visibly inserted on the page, and the published warning supplies the mathematical reason. The audit does not manufacture a new counterexample without reproducing its full crystalline logarithm calculation.
worth: Settled but essential editorial work: preserve the inserted hypotheses in every later use.

title: Fibration multiplicativity and local-system finiteness
as_he_states: Prove the local-system Euler lemma needed by the fibration spectral sequence; later ask whether the relative-polyhedral restriction can be omitted within E_infinity.
plausible_today: Finite CW homotopy type of the base is sufficient for ordinary Euler multiplicativity with finite-total-cohomology fibre. A compact-support theorem needs its own support/direct-image hypotheses. Constant-coefficient finiteness alone is insufficient.
state_of_art: Morin1962 Lemma1 gives the finite-cell local-system complex. West1977 Corollary5.3 supplies finite homotopy type for the compact ANRs arising under the specified cone interpretation. The telescope counterexample fully refutes only the broad provisional ordinary version.
why_open: The text explicitly identifies the local-system gap and later narrows the base; that is a mathematical correction in the manuscript itself.
worth: Worth reconstructing the final conical-case argument with all support comparisons; one run can complete the finite-type ordinary case and expose the remaining compact-support inputs.

title: The finite-cover alternative to cellular finiteness
as_he_states: Use arbitrarily fine finite covers with finite intersections to prove the local-system Euler lemma and its homological ordinary analogue.
plausible_today: Require a finite excisive cover or an acyclic resolution computing the chosen cohomology and refine it to trivialize the local system; finite intersection cohomology alone must be connected to that resolution.
state_of_art: Verdier1973 provides the support setting and Morin1962 the established finite-cell sufficient condition. The precise ambiguous cover-label formulation was not located as a named theorem in the searched primary sources.
why_open: The page states a route without writing the cover spectral sequence or the required comparison hypotheses.
worth: Worth a short technical lemma once the cover convention is fixed; start with open good covers and then test the manuscript’s closed-cover reading.

title: Triangulation of recursive conical spaces
as_he_states: List low-dimensional conical models, cancel a compact dimension-three triangulation clause, and doubt compact triangulation in dimension four.
plausible_today: Separate finite CW homotopy type from homeomorphic triangulation and manifold links from arbitrary singular links. Compact metric conical spaces have finite homotopy type under the recursive interpretation; compact4-manifolds need not be triangulable.
state_of_art: West Corollary5.3 proves the homotopy-finiteness input. Manolescu2015 §2.2 records Moise’s3-manifold theorem and the E8 four-dimensional obstruction. The exact broad singular-link low-dimensional triangulation claim remains a source/proof gap in this audit.
why_open: Pro records the deletion; Codex fails to mark it, so scans must settle the editorial discrepancy. No motive for the deletion is assigned.
worth: Worth checking the definitions and deletion first; further work should target a precise singular-link theorem rather than invoke Moise indiscriminately.

title: The compact conical core
as_he_states: Verify that cutting away an open half-cone leaves a compact conical member and that the punctured space retracts onto it.
plausible_today: With compact recursive links stable under joins, the boundary charts and explicit radial homotopy prove the two claims.
state_of_art: The local cone-product argument and radial formula are independently supplied in proof_checks.md; West applies only after the compact-metric ANR hypotheses are checked. No scan decision is implied about C/E notation.

title: Axiomatic uniqueness on E_infinity
as_he_states: Ask whether the first five axioms determine the Euler functions on every object of E_infinity; the separate main statement asserts existence.
plausible_today: Affirmative under the compact-metric recursive-cone interpretation: compactification and core have finite CW homotopy models, and subtraction at the compactification point determines compact supports.
state_of_art: West Corollary5.3 plus Morin’s finite-cell calculation gives the conditional modern completion written in proof_checks.md. A wider category without those hypotheses is not claimed settled.
why_open: The author explicitly says he does not know uniqueness; the manuscript supplies no finite-homotopy-type theorem.
worth: High interest and high feasibility: write the exact definition and dependency proof; this can become a clean self-contained companion result.

title: First Postnikov class of a loop space
as_he_states: For X=Omega Y, question a zero after k1∈H³(pi1,pi2) and draw possible successive cohomology-suspension lifts.
plausible_today: The ambient group need not vanish, and one loop does not force the class to vanish. Two compatible loopings force the first class to vanish, but do not give a natural splitting in the original space.
state_of_art: Arlettaz2000 Theorem7.6/Corollary7.7 prove double-loop vanishing/splitting; the1990 article’s publisher record dates receipt9June1987 and revision15April1988, publicationJanuary1990. Baues–Conduché1995 Theorem1.9 forbids a natural splitting; §§4–5 realize the independently checked single-loop counterexample.
why_open: The leaf is a scratch diagram with no proof. The supplied text does not determine which vanishing was intended, so this remains an ink/grammar question even though the alternatives have different mathematical answers.
worth: Worth a short annotated diagram explaining the three distinct assertions and the extra delooping hypothesis.

title: Denominators of the analytic differential invariant
as_he_states: Show that a rational differential expression regular on all étale coordinate pairs has denominator only a monomial in first derivatives.
plausible_today: For a universal finite-jet rational function over a coefficient domain, poles restricted to a1b1=0 force the reduced denominator to divide a power of a1b1. One must justify the passage from variable analytic coefficients to that universal jet statement.
state_of_art: The localized-polynomial-ring argument is independently given in proof_checks.md. DeligneI§5 supplies the actual third-order cocycle, but not this classification of all admissible expressions. Searches found no exact additional theorem matching the printed coefficient convention.
why_open: The source explicitly says this ought to be shown; the normalization of the jet-function category is left implicit.
worth: Worth a small algebraic lemma plus a jet-realization lemma; this is the first concrete step toward the larger classification.

title: Analytic uniqueness and redundancy of local surjectivity
as_he_states: Every admissible cocycle should be a nowhere-zero scalar multiple of G; étale naturality should make the scalar universal, and rigidity axiom d should imply local surjectivity e.
plausible_today: Fix finite jet order, rationality, analytic sheaf naturality and projective invariance, then prove a precise relative jet-group cocycle classification. Scalar constancy is a final step after classification, not its substitute.
state_of_art: Bouarroudj–Ovsienko1998 §1.2 gives the smooth Diff+(S1), PSL2-relative uniqueness. Ovsienko1993 recalls continuous real-line cohomology. Deligne proves the particular analytic torsor. None by itself proves all the manuscript’s local-complex operator quantifiers; the2025 MO thread was a search lead only.
why_open: The page asserts the classification while marking the redundant-axiom step as something to verify; no historical explanation is documented.
worth: High mathematical interest, medium feasibility: a few hours can fix the category and classify low jet orders, but should not promise the unrestricted theorem.

title: Integral universal uniqueness of G0
as_he_states: The integral Hasse operator should have coefficients in Z and be unique up to sign under the universal conditions.
plausible_today: Separate the proved integral cocycle identity from a universal recipient/classification statement; specify base change, locality, finite jet order, target module and surjectivity/generation. Only then do units of Z give the sign ambiguity.
state_of_art: The integral construction and characteristic2/3 tests are certified in a_computations.py. Deligne’s theta=S/6 explains characteristic-zero normalization. Classical relative smooth cohomology supplies an analogue, while no exact all-base theorem matching the printed quantifiers was located. Companion claimsC201–203 treat distinct coherent-target/fixed-p formulations.
why_open: The source offers a formula and examples, but no classification argument. Later nearby question marks and counterexamples concern different quantifier choices and must not be collapsed into this statement.
worth: Highest-interest algebraic direction: formulate the universal jet-group problem and compute its low-order module over Z before making an all-base uniqueness claim.
